think.script:
Welcome to Metric Market! It's Market Day, and Amy wants to open her juice stand.

[ON SCREEN: Market Day board]

But the Smudge mixed up the whole town. The Market Day board right under me has five jobs. Each one uses today's math.

[ON SCREEN: Three planks]

Here's the first puzzle. Mo is building Amy's counter out of three planks, end to end. Each plank is 1 meter 65 centimeters long. How long is the whole counter?

[ON SCREEN: The big question]

That length has two units in it, meters and centimeters. So how do we add or multiply an amount like that? Don't wait for me to show you. Try it your way first, on the Think About It bar. Write down how you did it. On the Learn tab, the Math Crew will show you two ways, and you can see if one matches yours.

learn.label: Learn · two ways on the mat
learn.title: Two Ways
learn.script:
Let's find the length of Amy's counter two ways.

[ON SCREEN: Board: The counter]

[DRAW: trace around the whole bar, then tap the question mark.]

Here are Mo's three planks, end to end. Each one is 1 meter 65 centimeters. The whole bar is the counter, and that's our question.

[ON SCREEN: Live: The mat]

[DO: build one plank: 1 meter, six 10s, five 1s. Tap + Add plank 2, then + Add plank 3. Then tap Trade 10 for 1 under the 1 cm column, and again under the 10 cm column.]

This is the Two-Unit Mat. I build one plank: 1 meter, six tens, five ones. Then two more planks. Look at the small columns: 15 ones and 18 tens. That's Atlas's way: 3 meters and 195 centimeters. But 195 centimeters is more than a meter, so I trade. Ten 1s for a 10. Ten 10s for a meter. 4 meters 95 centimeters!

[ON SCREEN: Board: Two ways]

[DRAW: fill in Atlas's blanks as you say them, then Felix's.]

Here are both ways on paper. Atlas splits the units: 3 meters and 195 centimeters, then regroups to 4 meters 95 centimeters.

Felix changes to one unit first. 1 meter 65 centimeters is 165 centimeters. 3 times 165 is 495 centimeters. Change back: 4 meters 95 centimeters. Same answer!

Pick the way that makes sense to you. Then build the counter on your mat.

do.label: Do · watch me solve (boards)
do.title: Watch Me Solve It
do.where: Learn, after the Market Measures Board
do.script:
Now watch me solve three. Pause any time.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 1]

[DRAW: write 1 | 75 in row 1 and again in row 2. Add down: 2 | 150. Cross out 100 cm, write +1 m: 3 | 50.]

Two times 1 meter 75 centimeters. I write one plank, then the same plank again. Add the meters: 2. Add the centimeters: 150. 150 is more than 100, so I trade 100 centimeters for 1 meter. 3 meters 50 centimeters.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 2]

[DRAW: write 4 | 300 on top and 1 | 600 under it. Cross out 4, write 3; cross out 300, write 1,300. Subtract each column: 2 | 700.]

4 kilograms 300 grams minus 1 kilogram 600 grams. 300 minus 600 won't work. So I regroup a kilogram: 3 kilograms 1,300 grams. 1,300 minus 600 is 700. 3 minus 1 is 2. 2 kilograms 700 grams. Felix checks it in grams: 4,300 minus 1,600 is 2,700. Same.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Spot the mistake]

[DRAW: circle 83 g. Write 8 kg = 8,000 g, then 8,003 g.]

Is this right? 8 kilograms is 8,000 grams. Plus 3 grams is 8,003. Not 83! The zeros hold the places. Watch for that on Millie's flour.

wrap.script:
Look how far you came!

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]

Today you worked with amounts that have two units. You can split the units and regroup, or change it all to one unit first. Both give the same answer.

[ON SCREEN: The sign]

And that Liter Well sign? 1 liter is 1,000 milliliters, so 2 liters is 2,000, not 200. Press Play and fix it so Amy can open. In clean mode, you'll fix it right on the page.

[ON SCREEN: Next time]

Next time we cross the Foot Bridge, where the trades are different: 12 inches make a foot. See you there, explorers!
